item.title: The Clerk, the gavel and 266 seats: the Fourteenth Assembly sits for the first time today — and can do nothing until it has a Speaker
item.description: The Order Paper for Friday carries a single line of business: the election of the Speaker and two deputies. Until that is done, the expanded National Assembly — 226 constituency seats and 40 proportional-representation seats created by the 2025 amendments — cannot transact anything at all. The President opens the session next Friday.

item.title: Home to the K31.46 morning: Hichilema lands from Abu Dhabi with US$2.14 billion in commitments — and says more is being finalised
item.description: The President returned to Kenneth Kaunda International Airport on Thursday evening quoting a figure of more than US$2.1 billion from his Abu Dhabi working visit — health, agriculture, tourism and energy, with a 100-hectare health city among the plans — while the forum's own count of signed instruments ran higher still. He arrived to the first full day of the new fuel prices.

item.title: Six aboard, no survivors: the Marondera helicopter crash that killed Wicknell Chivayo — and the DNA wait now holding the region's attention
item.description: Zimbabwe police confirm six people were aboard the helicopter that went down at Kudenga Farm near Marondera on Wednesday evening; the civil aviation authority's preliminary account says the tail struck first. Identification of the victims awaits DNA analysis. Tributes have come from Presidents Mnangagwa and Ruto — and the story has been followed as closely in Lusaka as in Harare.

item.title: Solar rows and a copper shaft: Britain's Africa trade commissioner ends a five-day Zambia pitch today
item.description: Alastair Long's Zambia programme closes on Friday after a week that took the UK Trade Commissioner for Africa from a GreenCo solar site to First Quantum's Trident mine — with the Green Growth Compact and British International Investment's strategy doing the framing, and a Terzeon reception doing the networking.

item.title: K3.3 billion in the furrows: on the eve of planting season, Indo Zambia Bank reveals the biggest farm book in its history
item.description: The bank's agriculture portfolio has reached K3.3 billion, it disclosed this week — K400 million of it through the smallholder facility that has reached more than 3,600 farmers — with earmarks behind it for soybeans, wheat and energy, timed to the season that starts with the first rains.

item.title: Day one at K31.46: the commuter arithmetic of a 24-per-cent jump, a kwacha at K19.61 — and December's VAT question
item.description: The first full day of the new pump prices dawned on the ranks and the filling stations with fares yet to move. But the arithmetic has moved: at long-distance consumption rates, the diesel line alone adds about K820 to a one-way Lusaka–Ndola run — and the VAT reinstatement dated for 1 December is still in the post.

item.title: 739 bags of suspected fake fertiliser, four men in custody: the DEC unearths an unregistered plant weeks before planting
item.description: The Drug Enforcement Commission has uncovered a manufacturing operation spanning 9 Miles and Meanwood Vorna Valley, seizing 739 bags of suspected counterfeit fertiliser, raw materials and equipment. An agricultural consultant and three businessmen face charges including money laundering — and the timing, at the gates of the planting season, is the point.

item.title: 304 cases, eleven dead, seven districts: Zambia declares a cholera outbreak weeks after the last one was declared over
item.description: Eight of the eleven deaths happened in the community — people reaching care too late. Acting Health Minister Gilbert Siame declared the outbreak on Wednesday: 304 cases across five provinces as of Tuesday, with Lusaka and Chibombo carrying the heaviest loads and a vaccination decision under assessment.

item.title: Ten matches, one kick-off: the Transition League begins tomorrow — champions Power Dynamos open at Konkola Blades
item.description: Every opening-round fixture kicks off at 15:00 on Saturday in a season built to move Zambian football's calendar: two streams drawn from last season's final standings, a new national cup alongside, and the champions beginning their defence in Chililabombwe.

item.title: Derulo at the Polo Field, thirty countries at the Showgrounds: a diary for a city in jacaranda season
item.description: Saturday belongs to the big stages: Jason Derulo headlines the Stanbic Music Festival from half past noon while the Diplomatic Fun Fair fills the Showgrounds. Beyond the weekend, October is stacked — theatre turns forty in Chingola, Barefeet turns twenty, and the virtual festival runs all month.

item.title: K31.46 at the pump: the tax holiday ends, excise returns — and Zambia wakes to its steepest fuel-price jump of the year
item.description: No statutory instrument appeared before midnight, so the six-month fuel-tax relief died on schedule. The Energy Regulation Board's October review restores excise duty and passes on dearer oil and a weaker kwacha: petrol up 24 per cent to K31.46, diesel up 24 to K33.27 — with VAT's return dated for 1 December.

item.title: “Instruments of justice and service, not sources of fear”: the Catholic bishops and the CCZ close ranks on the state of the nation
item.description: In separate but aligned statements on one Wednesday, Zambia's two largest church bodies questioned the credibility of the 2026 elections, decried arbitrary arrests and force that has cost civilian lives, and demanded an independent investigation into the killing of former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya. October, the bishops declared, will be a month of rosary prayers for peace.

item.title: “The outcome was never in doubt — the process is”: Antonio Mwanza gives the ECZ three questions, and a warning about 2031
item.description: The Democratic Progressive Party leader accepts that President Hichilema won — and says that is precisely why the Electoral Commission must now account for the suspended count, Mandevu's stolen ballots and a dead election agent. His prescription: commissioners chosen independently, a timetable that binds the incumbent, and public media that covers everyone.

item.title: Two hundred and fifty basis points: the Bank of Zambia delivers its biggest cut in more than a decade
item.description: Economists expected twenty-five. The Monetary Policy Committee delivered two hundred and fifty, taking the policy rate to 10.75 per cent — a fourth consecutive cut, powered by 6.1 per cent inflation, a record maize harvest and a firmer kwacha. The committee's own risk list, though, reads like next month's news.

item.title: K212 billion for creditors: the Green Paper prices the new term — and debt service outbids FISP, CDF and free education combined
item.description: The 2027–2029 Medium-Term Budget Plan, the Treasury's first blueprint of the new mandate, sets aside K212.2 billion for debt service — K63.6 billion more than the entire transfers budget for farmers, constituencies, pupils and school meals. The bill falls as a share of GDP only if the growth promises are true.

item.title: The Fund is back in town: Zambia opens successor-programme talks — and wants a deal before the year ends
item.description: An IMF mission led by Edward Gemayel is in Lusaka until 10 October, negotiating a successor to the US$1.7 billion programme that ended in January. The government is selling growth; the Fund is checking the sustainability file. Both are reading the same Green Paper.

item.title: “Not the Judiciary — the security services”: the State's answer for the three days the courts went dark
item.description: Attorney-General Mulilo Kabesha has told the Constitutional Court that August's closure of the courts was ordered by the defence and national security services, and merely communicated by the Judiciary. The admission — the first official attribution of responsibility — comes as the State asks that the Chapter One Foundation petition be dismissed with costs.

item.title: Five more carcasses in Nabwalya, twenty-six people on the register: the anthrax response races the river
item.description: Three more hippos and two more elephants have died of anthrax in the Nabwalya Game Management Area, taking the wildlife toll to 49 hippos, nine elephants and six buffaloes. Twenty-six human cases have now been reported — and investigators keep finding evidence that people are reaching the carcasses first.

item.title: 0.2 seconds at 18:21: ZESCO explains the night Levy Mwanawasa went dark — and promises new lights
item.description: The blackout that stopped Zambia's 2-0 win over Togo for eighteen minutes lasted, on the utility's account, a fifth of a second. The floodlights simply could not forgive it: their design demands about twenty minutes to return to full brightness. ZESCO will now engage the Ministry of Youth, Sport and Arts on a redesign.

item.title: Ten years of the Lusaka July — in October: “The Tale of a Ruby” opens at the National Museum on the 16th
item.description: The capital's most dressed-up weekend has a theme, a date and a tenth birthday. Lusaka July 2026 runs 16–18 October across three signature events, opening with a Night of Culture at the Lusaka National Museum — the social season's anchor, transplanted to the year's busiest cultural month.

item.title: Two billion for a Medical City, a challenge for Mopani and a pact still unsigned: Hichilema's US$2.14 billion day in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Memoranda worth US$2.14 billion were signed at the Zambia-UAE Business Forum on Tuesday, anchored by a US$2 billion plan to build a Medical City in Lusaka. The President also told Mopani's Emirati owners that the three-million-tonne copper target needs more of their ore — and left the biggest document, a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, for another day.

item.title: A night at Chimbokaila, a day of paperwork, then a smile at the gate: the Archbishop walks free on bail
item.description: The Archbishop of Lusaka spent Monday night in the capital's best-known correctional facility while his lawyers worked the bail conditions through the system. Late on Tuesday afternoon the gates opened, and the country's most watched defendant walked out smiling — to high-fives, handshakes and a Church that had barely slept.

item.title: Fourteen vacancies, one date: Mandevu, Lumezi North and Mbala vote again on 5 November — with August's ghosts on the ballot
item.description: The Electoral Commission has set Thursday, 5 November for two parliamentary by-elections, a mayoral race and eleven ward polls across five provinces. Mandevu's fresh vote is the residue of an attack on its own totalling centre; Lumezi North and Mbala are voting because death took their candidates within days of the election.

item.title: Sixty-five kwacha in every hundred never came back: government freezes the 2026 CDF loan window and turns collector
item.description: The empowerment-loan arm of the Constituency Development Fund — the cheap money aimed at youths, women, persons with disabilities and marketeers — is shut for 2026. The ministry says only 35 per cent of what has been lent since 2021 has been repaid, and new borrowers will now be funded only from what defaulters return.

item.title: Midnight, and still no signature: the fuel-tax holiday lapses tonight — and the ERB's October numbers follow within hours
item.description: Unless a statutory instrument appears in the next few hours, the excise suspension and VAT zero-rating that have kept two lines of the pump-price build-up blank since April die at midnight. The October review — the first in six months with the full tax load back in the formula — lands on the same midnight.

item.title: Turkish Airlines is leaving Lusaka's map — and an economist says the route is the least of what departs with it
item.description: The carrier has removed Lusaka from its future schedules for good. Kelvin Chisanga's warning is about what goes with it: investor access, tourist arrivals, and a piece of the country's argument — made again in Abu Dhabi this week — that Zambia is open for business.

item.title: K50, sausages and pens: the Lumezi South petition puts a farm linked to the Archbishop inside an election fight
item.description: The losing UPND candidate in Lumezi South wants a recount or a nullification — and his testimony alleges voters were given money and gifts at a farm associated with Archbishop Alick Banda, with instructions to vote for Brian Mundubile and Oliver Mwale. Under cross-examination, he conceded he has no pictures.

item.title: A US$2 billion city on paper, a Brazilian delegation in the corridor and a mine's K5.7 million: health's week of promises
item.description: The Medical City memorandum signed in Abu Dhabi is the largest health promise Zambia has ever heard. In the same week, smaller and more provable ones arrived — a pharmaceutical delegation from Brazil, a hospital upgrade from a mine, steady drug stocks in Chipangali. The gap between the two scales is where the health system actually lives.

item.title: Two goals, one blackout and a weight lifted: Zambia beat Togo 2-0 and turn Group I into a contest
item.description: Albert Kangwanda scored inside three minutes, the floodlights failed for twenty, and Eliya Mandanji finished it in stoppage time. Zambia's first win of the campaign draws them level with Togo on three points — and turns November's double-header with Burundi into the decider it was always going to be.

item.title: Free entry, thirty countries, one Saturday: the Diplomatic Fun Fair joins Lusaka's biggest weekend of the year
item.description: The Ministry of Tourism has launched the 2026 Diplomatic Fun Fair for 3 October at the Lusaka Showgrounds — the same Saturday Jason Derulo headlines the polo fields. For the capital's cultural economy, it is the busiest weekend on record.

item.title: The Archbishop in the dock: Banda denies the Hilux charge, wins K80,000 bail — and learns the State will try him on 3 November
item.description: The morning began with a solidarity Mass at the Cathedral of the Child Jesus. By afternoon the Archbishop of Lusaka had been formally arrested, charged and taken before a magistrate, where he pleaded not guilty. Bail came with sureties, surrendered travel documents — and, by Tuesday morning, reports that he was still in custody while the paperwork was done.

item.title: Solidarity, condemnation and a call for calm: Zambia absorbs the arrest of an archbishop
item.description: The bishops spoke of dignity and due process. The opposition spoke of persecution. The State spoke of evidence. And somewhere between the three, a country that has been arguing about its institutions all year found the argument distilled into a single courtroom.

item.title: While Lusaka watched a courtroom, the President landed in Abu Dhabi — and Haimbe told the UN that Zambia is stable and open
item.description: Day one of the UAE working visit puts a bilateral meeting, MoUs and an investment forum on the President's schedule. In New York, the foreign minister has already delivered the companion message: constitutionalism intact, Human Rights Council candidacy live, and the Grow Zambia Agenda open for partners.

item.title: Off the streets by today: Lusaka's vendors face the council's deadline — and a market system that must now absorb them
item.description: The Lusaka City Council's directive ordering street vendors back into designated markets takes effect today, with non-compliant traders warned they could lose their allocated spaces altogether. Enforcement will be watched block by block — and so will the question of whether the markets have room.

item.title: Thirty-six hours and no word: the fuel-tax waiver enters its final day-and-a-half, and the October price review waits on a signature
item.description: No statutory instrument, no ministerial statement, no gazette — as of this morning, the excise holiday and VAT zero-rating that have subsidised every litre since April still die at midnight tomorrow. The ERB's October review is being assembled in that silence.

item.title: Nineteen forty-nine and holding: the kwacha drifts into the fuel decision on a copper tailwind
item.description: The local unit closed last week stronger and opened this one around K19.49 to the dollar — nearly 19 per cent firmer than a year ago. In a week when the fuel cushion may lapse, the exchange rate is the one variable in the pump-price formula still working for the consumer.

item.title: Possession, suspicion and a satisfactory account: what Section 319 actually requires the State to prove against Archbishop Banda
item.description: The charge against the Archbishop is one of the Penal Code's most unusual offences — it turns not on theft, but on an explanation. With trial set for 3 November, here is what the prosecution must establish, what the defence is likely to argue, and why the five-year-old paper trail of a blue Hilux matters more than the politics around it.

item.title: Twenty-one human cases in Muchinga, a ministry correction in Southern — and 600,000 vaccine doses moving: inside Zambia's anthrax response
item.description: The active front of the outbreak is the Munyamadzi river system in Mpika, where human cases keep ticking up and hippo carcasses keep surfacing. In Southern Province, the government has spent a week knocking down a scarier number. Both stories say something about how the country handles a zoonosis it has met before.

item.title: Six o'clock in Ndola: a winless streak, a quiet coach's promise and the night that decides what this qualifying campaign is
item.description: Zambia host Togo at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium at 18:00 CAT — bottom of Group I against joint-top, nine matches without a win, and a coach who says the table can still be changed. By 20:00, the campaign has either restarted or gone very quiet.

item.title: The rigs are up, the sponsors are in, the Golden Circle is gone: Lusaka counts down to Derulo Saturday
item.description: With four days to the Stanbic Music Festival, silver sponsors are still signing on, the organisers' tiers are selling through, and the city's showgrounds economy is in its busiest week of the year. Saturday at Polo Field A is now a test of demand as much as a concert.

item.title: Mass at eight, the DEC at ten: Archbishop Banda answers a renewed summons over a five-year-old Hilux — and the Church walks him to the door
item.description: The Catholic Archbishop of Lusaka is due before Drug Enforcement Commission investigators this morning, nine months after he was warned and cautioned — and stayed silent — in the same investigation. The case is a Toyota Hilux once registered to the Zambia Revenue Authority. The context is a country arguing about whether its institutions are being turned on its critics.

item.title: 'Speaking out is citizenship, not rebellion': Brian Matambo's 31-minute reckoning with five years of looking away
item.description: In a Sunday video address accompanying a documentary titled 'Silence Brought Us Here', the Tonse Alliance figure traces a line from the peaceful 2021 handover to the treason arrests of 2026 — and tells Zambians the boundary moved because nobody pushed back.

item.title: Abu Dhabi tomorrow, New York today: Hichilema takes the Grow Zambia pitch to the Gulf as Haimbe addresses the UN
item.description: The President begins a two-day working visit to the UAE on Tuesday — bilateral talks, MoUs and an investment forum on the agenda — hours after his foreign minister delivers Zambia's national statement to the UN General Assembly in New York.

item.title: 'What message is he sending to the younger generation?': Chief Choongo rebukes Dr Kalumba — and explains why chiefs stand with the government of the day
item.description: The Monze traditional leader and former House of Chiefs chairperson calls the former minister's remarks about the President disappointing and un-Zambian, telling a country deep in a quarrel about dissent that the campaign season is over.

item.title: One day of relief left: the fuel-tax waiver dies at midnight tomorrow, Lusaka has said nothing — and the October price review is already in the room
item.description: The excise-duty holiday and VAT zero-rating that have subsidised every litre since April lapse on 30 September. No statutory instrument has been gazetted, no minister has spoken, and the ERB's October review — due within days — will be the first to price fuel without knowing whether the cushion exists.

item.title: Copper declared as cement: Avocado Mining admits attempted smuggling — and its K100,000 fine falls due the day after tomorrow
item.description: The Kalulushi-based miner pleaded guilty to ten counts over a 2025 attempt to export K23.9 million of copper concentrate labelled as Portland cement. In a separate operation, ZRA seized two brand-new Land Cruisers misclassified at the border — a Sunday statement that reads as a warning shot to the whole clearing trade.

item.title: Candles at the Cancer Diseases Hospital: September closes with a vigil — and a survival target Zambia has four years to meet
item.description: At a Friday evening vigil marking Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, the Ministry of Health put the country's position plainly: about 400,000 children worldwide develop cancer each year, most in low- and middle-income countries — and Zambia has promised to help push survival to 60 per cent by 2030.

item.title: Bronze for the juniors, a three-peat for Amajita: Zambia leave Maputo with a medal as South Africa take the crown again
item.description: Gift Mumbi and a Sipho Muntanga double beat Namibia 3-0 in Sunday's third-place play-off, before South Africa retained the regional title 2-1 against the hosts — a fifth straight win that sends both finalists to Ghana 2027, and sends Zambia home with pride intact but no ticket.

item.title: The eve of the must-win: a recovery session, a quiet stadium and a Tuesday night that could define the qualifying campaign
item.description: Twenty-four hours before Togo arrive at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium, Zambia's squad is managing its wounds from Algeria and the federation is still selling tickets. The table is not complicated: the visitors are level at the top, the hosts are bottom, and November's fixtures get very dark if Tuesday goes wrong.

item.title: Golden Circle gone, Saturday looms: Jason Derulo comes to the Polo Field — and Lusaka's big-show economy takes another step
item.description: The Stanbic Music Festival returns on 3 October with its biggest headline booking yet: Jason Derulo, one night only, at Polo Field A. Golden Circle tickets are already sold out — VIP and standard remain — in a week that has made Lusaka's international concert calendar feel suddenly permanent.

item.title: Twenty-nine days, one court bus, no plea: Mundubile and Zulu surface in Solwezi — and the case against them starts to take shape
item.description: Zambia's defeated presidential candidate and his running mate made their first court appearance since their August arrest, ferried across the country from Kabwe to face sedition charges over post-election Facebook posts. The treason case that jailed them has yet to reach a courtroom at all.

item.title: Arrested at dawn in Chienge, charged in Kabwe, bonded by evening: the two-day case against Dr Katele Kalumba
item.description: The former finance minister faces a cyber-harassment charge over an August post said to humiliate the President. The opposition calls the manner of his arrest an abduction; the ruling party says a man pardoned out of prison by this President should know better.

item.title: 'What is this hullabaloo?': Hichilema says there is no crisis — and tells social media they are scaring away the investors he fought to win
item.description: At a routine swearing-in on Friday the President delivered anything but a routine speech: a defence of the post-election climate, a warning that the law 'does not recognise age', and an appeal to Zambians at home and abroad to stop 'creating a crisis where there is none'.

item.title: Six passports cancelled, one seven-day ultimatum: Haimbe defends the exile-list from New York as Mutambo's lawyers count down to Monday
item.description: The Foreign Affairs Minister says withdrawing a passport is not withdrawing citizenship; the UK-based commentator's lawyers say the cancellation was unlawful, attributed to the wrong official and unexplained beyond two words: 'security reasons'. Court action is threatened if it is not restored within days.

item.title: The cushion expires on Tuesday: government still undecided on fuel-tax relief as the October price review looms
item.description: Since April, suspended excise duty and zero-rated VAT have quietly subsidised every litre sold in Zambia — at a cost of roughly $200 million a quarter in forgone revenue. The relief lapses on 30 September, and as of this weekend, Lusaka had not said whether it will be renewed.

item.title: 'Two-way impact': Zambia takes its Human Rights Council campaign to New York, with its record very much in the room
item.description: At a reception for UN member states, the President and his foreign minister asked the world to elect Zambia to the Human Rights Council for 2027–2029 — a bid that lands in the same week as an EU resolution on post-election repression and a defence of six cancelled passports.

item.title: 'Togo won't have it easy': home, hurt and already cornered — Lwandamina's Chipolopolo reach the must-win in Ndola
item.description: Back from Tizi Ouzou with a 3-1 defeat, a bruised squad and a blunt table — Zambia bottom, Togo level with Algeria at the top — the interim coach is asking the Levy Mwanawasa crowd to turn one match into a rescue operation on Tuesday night.

item.title: One more morning in Maputo: Junior Chipolopolo play for bronze today as South Africa and Mozambique contest the crown
item.description: Two days after the 4-2 semi-final that slipped away, Zambia's youngsters face Namibia in the third-place play-off at ABB Stadium — a consolation match that doubles as an audition — before the hosts meet the holders for the regional title and the two Ghana 2027 tickets already booked.

item.title: Number 10 in Denmark: Mercy Chipasula, 18, takes the Copper Queens pipeline to HB Køge
item.description: The Kitwe-born forward who captained Zambia's U17s and has already played two senior WAFCONs has signed for the Danish top-flight club — whose sporting director says they beat 'some of the biggest clubs in the world' to her signature.

item.title: The gates are open: Zambia's national parks are free to enter this weekend — and today is the last day
item.description: To mark World Tourism Day, the Ministry of Tourism waived entry fees at all 20 national parks on 26 and 27 September for citizens and school groups — a two-day invitation to see the estate the country keeps selling to the world.

item.title: 'Resist it': Laura Miti's third-term warning lands as Chapter One tells the President to say it plainly
item.description: Two of civil society's loudest voices moved within a day of each other — one telling Zambians to resist any third-term push before it starts, the other telling Hakainde Hichilema that only his own words can end the speculation.

item.title: 'A full-blown police state': Kateka says the security wings are being used to silence dissent — and claims the clampdown was planned before the vote
item.description: The New Heritage Party leader used a radio interview to accuse the UPND of winning 'with manipulation' and deploying the army where it had lost — claims the government has consistently rejected, and which observer missions have not substantiated.

item.title: Healing as homework: church leaders tell a divided country to pray — and to reconcile
item.description: At the Revival Prayer Network's Grand Thursday gathering in Lusaka, three church figures framed post-election reconciliation as the Church's assignment — not the state's alone.

item.title: 6.1 per cent: inflation grinds to an eight-year low — five days before the fuel-tax cushion expires
item.description: ZamStats' September print extends the disinflation run that returned the rate to the Bank of Zambia's 6–8 per cent band in February — but the monthly figure is the firmest in five months, and the tax measures cushioning fuel lapse on Tuesday.

item.title: Borrowing from the funeral grant, at zero per cent: 7,000 retirees have drawn K90 million from NAPSA's advance
item.description: The facility pays up to 75 per cent of a retiree's funeral grant while they are still alive — recovered in small deductions so the monthly pension keeps coming. Demand, says CEO Muyangwa Muyangwa, is growing daily.

item.title: Sixteen and a half thousand new cancers a year: the Cancer Diseases Hospital puts a number on the burden
item.description: Cervical cancer alone accounts for about 4,700 new cases annually and kills more than half of those it strikes, UTH's cancer hospital says — with only about 3,000 patients currently in treatment there.

item.title: 'The soil was loose and dangerous': a warned-off scramble for copper stones kills three illegal miners at KCM's OB-19 dump
item.description: Two teenagers and a 20-year-old died when a section of the Chingola dumpsite collapsed on Wednesday evening. Five were pulled out alive by fellow miners. Police have opened an inquiry — and repeated a familiar Copperbelt warning.

item.title: Sakala's riposte, then the desert cold: Zambia fall 3-1 in Tizi Ouzou as the winless run reaches nine
item.description: Fashion Sakala's 57th-minute equaliser briefly quietened the Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium, but Ibrahim Maza and Anis Hadj Moussa struck inside seven second-half minutes to give Ibrahim Hamdani a winning start — and leave Chipolopolo bottom of the group. Togo visit on Tuesday.

item.title: A lead, an equaliser, a red card, two penalties: Junior Chipolopolo's AFCON dream dies in a 4-2 Maputo classic
item.description: Zambia led holders South Africa at half-time and levelled again at 2-2 through Jonathan Kalimina — who was sent off moments later. Steven Mendes scored twice from the spot, Emile Witbooi sealed it late, and the 12-time champions miss out on Ghana 2027.

item.title: 'Take them to court or release them — you can't have it both ways': Laura Miti's ultimatum over the Kafwaya silence
item.description: A month after former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya died in a security operation, one of the country's best-known rights campaigners says the state's silence has left it exposed to the conclusion it fears most — an unlawful killing.

item.title: 'Beacon of democracy', with an asterisk: EU promises Zambia deeper ties and €110 million — and presses the rule of law
item.description: Commissioner Jozef Síkela's bilateral with Mulambo Haimbe in New York delivered budget support, a Global Gateway embrace and diplomatic relations with Andorra — while Brussels kept one eye on Kabwe.

item.title: The petition that ended with a handshake: Mwewa confirmed as Lusaka mayor after Kibombwe consents to withdraw
item.description: The Local Government Elections Tribunal has formally withdrawn Gabriel Kibombwe's challenge to the 13 August mayoral result — by the mutual consent of every party in the room — ending a month of legal shadow over City Hall.

item.title: Zanaco writes the rulebook: Zambia's first bank sustainability bond heads to market at $100 million
item.description: A $50 million private placement anchored by British International Investment's $15 million opens the programme — a transaction the Lusaka Securities Exchange calls a first for a Zambian bank, and a template it hopes others will copy.

item.title: Four hundred chemical engineers wanted: CBU and UCF sign lab deal ahead of a $1.5 billion fertiliser expansion
item.description: United Capital Fertilisers will help build a state-of-the-art chemical laboratory, lecture theatre and student accommodation at the Copperbelt University — and says its ammonia-urea plant expansion breaks ground within weeks.

item.title: Forty-six dead hippos, one confirmed case: what we actually know about the Muchinga anthrax outbreak
item.description: Laboratory evidence is lagging the carcass count in the Munyamadzi corridor. Zambia's national One Health coordinator says only one hippo death is lab-confirmed — and cautions against blaming anthrax for every dead animal.

item.title: Matchday in Tizi Ouzou: Chipolopolo open the road to AFCON 2027 against the Desert Foxes tonight
item.description: A rebuilt Zambia squad — completed by the late arrivals of Lungu and Liteta, and minus the withdrawn Andrew Sinkala — faces Algeria at the Hussein Aït Ahmed Stadium with a long winless run to snap.

item.title: Ninety minutes from Ghana: Junior Chipolopolo meet holders South Africa with an AFCON ticket on the line
item.description: Friday's 16:00 CAT semi-final in Maputo pits the region's two most decorated youth sides against each other — Zambia's twelve titles against Amajita's ten — with the finalists bound for the U20 AFCON in Ghana.

item.title: Silondwa survives three-way countback to lift Discover Insurance golf title at Nkana
item.description: Kedrick Silondwa's 42 points off a 12 handicap topped a tightly contested field at Nkana Golf Club, as the insurer marked its fourth anniversary with the championship.

item.title: The gate at Mukobeko stays shut: treason accused cut off from visitors as defence demands answers
item.description: Prison officers in Kabwe have turned away visitors to Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 co-accused, according to people familiar with the attempts — the latest front in a case where procedure has become the story.

item.title: 'Our diplomacy must help to grow Zambia': Haimbe works the UN corridors as two stories compete outside
item.description: Two new diplomatic relationships, a Human Rights Council bid and a national statement on Monday — while diaspora organisers and the foreign minister tell different stories about protests at the gates.

item.title: 'Two terms': the opposition is quoting Hichilema back at himself as the term-limits storm swirls
item.description: State House has repeatedly denied any third-term ambition. But with Tayali's campaign growing louder and the President yet to address it directly this week, his own past words have become the opposition's favourite document.

item.title: The kwacha at 19.5, inflation at an eight-year low: a week of deadlines for Zambia's economic managers
item.description: The currency has drifted softly this month while prices stay tame. Now three dates collide — the September inflation print, a monetary policy decision and the expiry of the fuel-tax moratorium.

item.title: KCM signs $498m deal to mine its own waste — the biggest tailings recovery plant in Africa
item.description: Vedanta's Zambian unit will extract 70,000 tonnes of copper a year from decades of Chingola tailings, as the metal's price and the country's three-million-tonne ambition keep climbing.

item.title: Twenty-two games unbeaten: Belmadi's Algeria await the Chipolopolo in Tizi Ouzou
item.description: George Lwandamina's first competitive match in charge is about as hard as African football gets — away to the Desert Foxes on Friday night, with Togo at home four days later.

item.title: Three wins, eight goals, one conceded: Junior Chipolopolo sweep Group C and meet the hosts on Friday
item.description: A 3-1 win over Botswana sealed a perfect group stage in Maputo. One more win — against Mozambique in the semi-final — puts Zambia at the Under-20 AFCON in Ghana.

item.title: The season of the stage: Stanbic festival returns as Kwacha Music Awards locks in November
item.description: Zambia's live-music calendar is stacking up — a bank-backed festival promising a star-studded local lineup, and the industry's biggest night set for 27 November.

item.title: The term-limits storm: Tayali wants the ceiling scrapped — civil society says don't you dare
item.description: Calls to scrap the presidential two-term limit have exploded into the open, with Chilufya Tayali leading the charge and civil society, opposition figures and a veteran constitutionalist warning of a third-term agenda.

item.title: Diaspora to protest at the UN as Haimbe arrives to defend Zambia's record
item.description: Zambians in the US plan a demonstration outside UN headquarters in New York this week over the disputed election and the killing of Mutotwe Kafwaya — days before Foreign Minister Haimbe delivers Zambia's national statement.

item.title: Masebo challenges Chongwe East result over alleged malpractice
item.description: Losing UPND candidate Sylvia Masebo has petitioned the Lusaka High Court over the Chongwe East parliamentary result — one of a string of election petitions now testing the 13 August outcomes.

item.title: 40 PR MPs sworn in as parliament widens — and watchdogs like what they see
item.description: Speaker Nelly Mutti has sworn in the 40 proportional-representation members reserved for women, youth and persons with disabilities — the first fruit of the amended constitution's new architecture.

item.title: More buyers eye Zambian maize as the record harvest goes to market
item.description: Regional demand is lining up for Zambia's surplus maize weeks after the 540,000-tonne Kenya deal — with the FRA insisting food security is ring-fenced before exports move.

item.title: Lusaka, Copperbelt and Eastern top syphilis infections, health data shows
item.description: New figures put the three most urbanised provinces at the top of the syphilis burden, with health officials urging testing and early treatment — especially in antenatal care.

item.title: Lungu and Liteta complete the squad as Chipolopolo eye Algeria
item.description: Gamphani Lungu and Liteta have arrived in camp to complete the Chipolopolo squad for the Algeria clash, though German-based Andrew Sinkala has been excused by FAZ.

item.title: Haalubono handed the Copper Queens reins for the Olympic battle
item.description: The Copper Queens have a new head coach as the federation turns its attention to the Olympic qualification campaign — a promotion from within for a programme that plans long cycles.

item.title: Short film, long shadow: Lusaka's festival wraps a breakout edition
item.description: The Lusaka Short Film Festival has concluded after screenings that drew new audiences to Zambian storytelling — another marker for a film scene building real momentum.

item.title: Lusaka rejects EU Parliament's post-election resolution as 'premature'
item.description: The European Parliament has called for an independent investigation into the killing of former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya and the post-election crackdown. Government says the resolution is premature and insufficiently informed.

item.title: Mafinga South MP Faith Munthali critically ill after alleged abduction
item.description: The newly elected MP is in Isoka General Hospital after what her family and party describe as an abduction. Police have been asked to investigate; details remain thin and contested.

item.title: Honeybee case reopens: court clears DPP's appeal against Chilufya acquittal
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Court has ruled the Director of Public Prosecutions' appeal against the acquittal of former health minister Chitalu Chilufya in the Honeybee defective-drugs case can proceed.

item.title: Arrows stun Power Dynamos to lift the Charity Shield
item.description: Red Arrows upset league champions Power Dynamos to win the season-opening Charity Shield — an early marker in what promises to be a fierce title race.

item.title: Mpundu accuses Tembo of betrayal as cracks widen in the Tonse Alliance
item.description: Tonse Alliance chairman Binwell Mpundu has publicly accused Ezra Tembo of betraying those who built his career — the loudest rupture yet inside the opposition since the August defeat.

item.title: Hichilema hosts the Duchess of Edinburgh as royal visit spotlights education
item.description: President Hichilema met Sophie, the Duchess of Edinburgh, during her visit to Zambia — a diplomatic bright spot in a month dominated by post-election tension.

item.title: Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others sue the State over their detention
item.description: The eighteen treason suspects have petitioned over alleged rights violations, saying they were moved from Mukobeko to Mwembeshi without a lawful warrant — the first major legal counterattack since the charges were laid.

item.title: Mass anthrax vaccination targets 20,000 animals in Muchinga
item.description: Government has launched a vaccination campaign covering 20,000 animals in Mpika, Shiwang'andu and Lavushimanda, with Mpika identified as the epicentre of the outbreak.

item.title: Daka double douses the Flames: Zambia 2-0 Malawi
item.description: Substitute Billy Daka came off the bench to score twice in the closing stages as the Chipolopolo beat Malawi — a statement win in front of home fans.

item.title: 'No cousin, no brother': Hichilema swears in his second-term cabinet with a warning
item.description: President Hakainde Hichilema has sworn in the first batch of his new cabinet at State House, telling ministers that delivery — not relationships — will decide who keeps their seat.

item.title: Treason case: Correctional Service denies blocking lawyers as Findlay's family raises health alarm
item.description: A dispute has erupted over legal access at Mukobeko — while Harry Findlay's family says his health is deteriorating in detention.

item.title: Tonse Alliance suspends Zimba — the dialogue call that cost him his job
item.description: Days after urging the opposition to recognise President Hichilema and pursue dialogue, secretary general Dr Chris Zumani Zimba has been suspended.

item.title: Former Education PS Henry Tukombe arrested over US$401 million contract
item.description: Anti-corruption officers have arrested the former Ministry of Education permanent secretary in connection with a US$401 million contract — one of the largest figures ever attached to a Zambian graft case.

item.title: Mwamba demands independent probe into officer's death at police headquarters
item.description: The Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance disputes the police account that Assistant Superintendent Daniel Banda took his own life.

item.title: Kenya signs for 540,000 tonnes of Zambian maize — the record harvest finds its market
item.description: The Food Reserve Agency has signed with Kenya's Baita Trading to export more than half a million tonnes of surplus maize.

item.title: Al Merrikh in Ndola as Power Dynamos chase a CAF comeback
item.description: Zambian champions Power Dynamos host Sudanese giants Al Merrikh needing to overturn a first-leg deficit.

item.title: Inflation eases to 9.2% as food prices stabilise — relief, with a footnote
item.description: The disinflation run continues toward single digits. The market stall will confirm when it arrives.

item.title: Hichilema presses Vedanta to fast-track power investment as copper ambitions outrun the grid
item.description: The president has urged Vedanta to accelerate power-generation plans, as fresh GreenCo funding signals the private build-out is moving.

item.title: Anthrax scare in Muchinga: what is confirmed, what is ruled out
item.description: Suspected anthrax recorded in Muchinga Province; Lavushimanda reports no livestock cases. What the evidence says so far.

item.title: Barbra Banda nominated for the Ballon d'Or — again
item.description: The Copper Queens and Orlando Pride striker is on the Ballon d'Or shortlist for another year.

item.title: Hichilema sworn in for a second term — and the economy is the whole speech
item.description: Hakainde Hichilema took the oath at National Heroes Stadium on Tuesday after winning 61.4% of the vote. His promise for term two: investment, jobs, and three times the copper.

item.title: Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and Findlay moved to Mukobeko as treason case widens to 18
item.description: Opposition leader Brian Mundubile, his running mate Makebi Zulu and businessman Harry Findlay have been transferred to Mukobeko Maximum Security Prison on treason charges, according to multiple reports.

item.title: Zumani Zimba breaks ranks: 'Zambia must choose dialogue over division'
item.description: Tonse Alliance secretary general Dr Chris Zumani Zimba has defied critics within his own camp to call for national dialogue — and even a government of national unity.

item.title: The kwacha is one of 2026's standout currencies. What does that buy you?
item.description: Up roughly 20% against the dollar in a year and trading near 19.1 to the greenback, the kwacha is riding copper and a record maize harvest.

item.title: Kopala showed up for Danny Kaya — and Lusaka got its turn this weekend
item.description: The eighth Danny Kaya Music Festival packed the Copperbelt before a moving tribute to the late Dandy Krazy.

item.title: September 30 is copper day: the export-duty decision that reveals Zambia's real bottleneck
item.description: Zambia extended its waiver on the 10% copper-concentrate export duty to the end of September while the country's biggest smelters sit in maintenance.

item.title: Zambia's copper boom runs on electricity the grid doesn't have yet
item.description: Reaching 3 million tonnes of copper needs at least 2,000 extra megawatts. The power deficit was 707MW last year — but Kariba is recovering.

item.title: Zesco Ndola Girls' COSAFA run ends in final defeat — 'we'll be back for the title'
item.description: A perfect group stage, a semi-final statement, then Mamelodi Sundowns in the final. Zesco Ndola Girls fell short — but announced themselves.

item.title: Veteran Refinery shutdown: what is confirmed, what is claimed, and what remains unanswered
item.description: The Copperbelt facility has halted operations under disputed circumstances. Allegations about the arrest of Mr. D. Nayek remain unverified.

item.title: Kangwa's Greek move and Lungu's injury race: the Chipolopolo European watch
item.description: Klings Kangwa unveiled by Panathinaikos after a Hall of Fame farewell, while Gamphani Lungu races an injury before AFCON preparations.

item.title: Fuel prices hold for September — and it's the suspended taxes doing the work
item.description: Petrol stays at K25.29 and diesel at K26.86 despite Middle East pressure on oil prices.

item.title: Inflation dips again to 6.2% — closing in on the target floor
item.description: Annual inflation eased to 6.2% in August, a new eight-year low, with mealie meal prices falling month-on-month — welcome data for a re-elected government with promises to keep.

item.title: Kabulonga operation: former minister Kafwaya killed, opposition figures detained
item.description: A security operation at a Lusaka property days after the vote left former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya dead in what police described as an exchange of fire, and led to the detention of senior opposition figures — including, reportedly, Brian Mundubile found at the scene.

item.title: Hichilema wins a second term with about 60% of the vote
item.description: The Electoral Commission declared Hakainde Hichilema re-elected with about 60.5% of the vote against Brian Mundubile's 37.9%, while the UPND took a commanding parliamentary majority.

item.title: Election day: 8.7 million registered voters go to the polls
item.description: Zambians voted on 13 August to choose a president, 226 constituency MPs, mayors and councillors — a vote framed as a referendum on the government's economic record.

item.title: Copper Queens wrap up pre-camp as preparations intensify
item.description: Zambia's women's national team concluded a local pre-camp in July as the technical team steps up preparations, with attention on the next generation joining the Barbra Banda core.

item.title: Hichilema switches on Chisamba II: 100 more megawatts of solar
item.description: The US$70 million second phase of the Chisamba solar plant was commissioned on 21 July, doubling the site to 200MW — a centrepiece of the drought-proofing energy push.

item.title: The reserves row: US$6.5 billion in the bank, and a campaign over who feels it
item.description: A debate over Zambia's record foreign-exchange reserves became the economic heart of the campaign, with Brian Mundubile asking what US$6.5 billion does for the cost of living — and Situmbeko Musokotwane answering.

item.title: The burial that became a campaign: Lungu's legacy shadows the race
item.description: A year after his death, the unresolved burial of former president Edgar Lungu has become one of the most emotive issues of the campaign, after Brian Mundubile promised a 'dignified burial' if elected.

item.title: Kwacha touches 18 to the dollar — strongest in nearly three years
item.description: The kwacha firmed to around K18.07 per US dollar in June, its strongest level since 2023, buoyed by copper earnings, reserves at about US$6.5 billion and renewed investor confidence.

item.title: Inflation falls to 6.5% — the lowest in eight years
item.description: Zambia's annual inflation rate eased to 6.5% in June 2026, a level last seen in February 2018, as the kwacha firmed and debt restructuring steadied the economy.

item.title: Justice minister moves to defer Bill 7 again
item.description: The Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Bill No. 7 was deferred once more in late June, with the Justice Ministry citing the need for further consultation on the divisive constitutional package.

item.title: Hichilema launches UPND manifesto: growth, jobs, free education
item.description: President Hichilema formally launched his re-election platform on 11 June, promising continued economic recovery, expanded free education and support for agriculture.
